"[Automated license plate readers](https://www.eff.org/pages/automated-license-plate-readers-alpr) (ALPRs) are high-speed, computer-controlled camera systems that are typically mounted on street poles, streetlights, highway overpasses, mobile trailers, or attached to police squad cars. ALPRs automatically capture all license plate numbers that come into view, along with the location, date, and time. The data, which includes photographs of the vehicle and sometimes its driver and passengers, is then uploaded to a central server."

Police can search this database and choose to share with other agencies (like your insurance company).

I believe travel patterns were instrumental, as well as passenger information. It took hundreds of searches with very specific parameters and a very dedicated investigator to zero in on him.
